events.title: New Amsterdam Surrenders to the English
events.description: Dutch authorities surrendered the colony of New Amsterdam to an English fleet without a fight. The English renamed it New York in honor of the Duke of York.
events.significance: The handover put the future New York City under English control and reshaped the colonial map of North America.

events.title: Congress Passes the Judiciary Act
events.description: The first U.S. Congress passed the Judiciary Act. It set up the federal court system and created the office of Attorney General.
events.significance: The act built the structure of the American federal judiciary, which still shapes how justice works in the United States.

events.title: The Poona Pact Is Signed
events.description: Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar reached an agreement in India on political representation for oppressed castes. It ended Gandhi's fast and replaced separate electorates with reserved seats in legislatures.
events.significance: The pact was a landmark in India's struggle over caste and political representation, and it influenced the country's later system of reserved seats.

events.title: Honda Motor Co. Is Founded
events.description: Mechanic and inventor Soichiro Honda founded the Honda Motor Company in postwar Japan.
events.significance: The small company grew into one of the world's largest makers of motorcycles and automobiles, and it became a symbol of Japan's postwar industrial rise.
